rows.answer: He treats computational functionalism as an unexamined assumption that "may be" wrong, not a proven falsehood [spya-wepmnr]. His central reason is that in brains you cannot separate what they do from what they are, the way software separates from hardware [spya-zw2m7u spya-p4vmm0]. steps.words: What does Seth mean by the 'mythology' of conscious AI?
computational functionalism assumption

rows.answer: He never defines the word, but uses it for the stories about conscious machines that we take on without checking them: biases that make us see minds where there are none [spya-k850tu], dreams of a "techno-rapture" and of living forever [spya-v4sduf spya-ryg483], all resting on an assumption he says is rarely examined [spya-wepmnr]. He links that rapture to the Cartesian soul, a mind fully separable from the body [spya-gvzuc4]. For the rest, read where he calls the techno-rapture "a regression to the Cartesian soul" [spya-gvzuc4].

steps.words: Is his argument against the brain-as-computer idea actually convincing?
neural replacement thought experiment

rows.answer: He rests it on three things: brains don't split cleanly into software and hardware [spya-zw2m7u]; some neurons fire to clear away metabolic waste [spya-un9fjn]; and brains run in continuous time, while an algorithm only cares about the order of its steps [spya-v2q8qk]. My guess: a functionalist would answer that only the level of detail that matters for consciousness has to be copied, a reply he doesn't take up when he dismisses the neuron-replacement thought experiment [spya-ahtr6e].
